title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities (including any director and other KMP), Senior Employees reporting directly to a KMP, any other person the Board designates in writing, and Connected Persons of the above.

tiers.name: KMP, Key Consultant, Key Contractor, Senior Employee, Other Employee (where applicable) (excluding Chief Executive Officer or Company Secretary)
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: Approving Officer is the Chief Executive Officer, alternate the Chair.

tiers.name: Director (excluding the Chair), Chief Executive Officer or Company Secretary
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: Approving Officer is the Chair, alternate the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: Approving Officer is the Board, no alternate.

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18, a parent, an unlisted body corporate of which you are a director, a trust of which you are trustee and of which you or the above is a beneficiary, or any other person over whom you have significant influence or control.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding in the Company

windows.end_anchor: 24 hours immediately following the release of the Company's quarterly cash flow report for that financial quarter

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may from time to time declare an Additional Period (for example because the Company is considering matters that would require disclosure but for Listing Rule 3.1A). Confidential: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.

rules.detail: Securities expressly includes derivatives (equity swaps, futures, hedges, exchange-traded or OTC options), cash or otherwise settled, with no venue limit. Trading such a derivative is a 'trade' and, under section 7, no Restricted Person may trade in Securities at any time without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise (Securities)

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route referenced, on arrangements limiting the economic risk of unvested entitlements under equity-based remuneration schemes.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person is prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: For security holdings other than unvested equity-scheme entitlements, hedging arrangements are expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
rules.evidence: Before entering into any transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding in the Company a Restricted Person must first obtain prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a 'trade' as an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of Securities, so it requires prior written clearance and could also be caught as a hedging arrangement under 9.1.
rules.evidence: to enter into an agreement to apply, for, acquire, or dispose of Securities or procure another person to do so

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy, unlike the 'short term or speculative trading' restriction in section 10, which addresses holding period rather than the borrow-and-sell practice.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named but fall within 'derivatives ... whether settled by cash or otherwise', so entering one over Securities requires prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise (Securities)

rules.detail: Margin loan agreements over Securities require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer; a subsequent forced sale by the lender is excluded from the Prohibited Period restrictions (section 8(d)).
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Granting security is captured as 'other secured lending arrangements' and requires the same prior written clearance as a margin loan; not addressed via the general trade/dealing definition.
rules.evidence: or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: Section 9.2 permits any secured lending arrangement over Securities with prior written clearance, with no stated exclusion by tier or vesting state.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Unconditional statement that Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading; unlike sections 9.1/9.2, no 'without first obtaining prior written clearance' carve-out is attached to this restriction.
rules.evidence: The Company wishes to encourage Restricted Persons to adopt a long term attitude to investment in Securities. Therefore, Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Securities.

exemption_authority: The relevant Approving Officer (Chief Executive Officer for KMP/Key Consultants/Key Contractors/Senior/Other Employees; Chair for Directors, the CEO or Company Secretary; the Board for the Chair) may grant prior written clearance to trade during a Prohibited Period for severe financial hardship or other circumstances they deem exceptional, in their sole and absolute discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not trade in Securities at any time (including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6) unless they first obtain prior written clearance from [the Approving Officer table].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is required for every dealing at any time, not just during Blackout or Additional Periods, so entry, unwind and settlement of a collar each need fresh 5-business-day clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Prohibited Period ban, giving a workable enforcement path even during a blackout or confidential Additional Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Before entering into any transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding ... clearance ... A Restricted Person is prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is only categorically barred while the underlying shares are unvested scheme entitlements; once vested, hedging (and by extension a collar) is expressly permitted subject to clearance, unlike policies with a blanket hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary will maintain a register of clearances given in accordance with this section 7, and must report all clearances given to the Board at its next following meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike comparable policies, NMG does not appear to require the Restricted Person to confirm trade details after dealing, reducing post-execution administrative friction for the bank's collar settlement, though clearance withdrawal risk (below) remains.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Written clearance may be withdrawn by the Approving Officer at any time during the clearance period should the Approving Officer consider that the circumstances have changed, having regard to the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed trading in Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar transaction can be pulled by the Approving Officer for broad reputational or governance reasons even within the 5-business-day validity window, before the trade is executed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Restricted Person dealing in Securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle ... that happens to hold ... Securities in the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms indirect exposure via pooled vehicles is not itself regulated dealing, though a bespoke bilateral OTC collar with a bank would not qualify for this carve-out.

summary: A funded collar over vested NMG shares is achievable, but every element needs prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer (CEO, Chair, or Board depending on role), because Securities expressly includes exchange-traded and OTC derivatives and section 7 requires clearance for all trading at any time. The hedging ban in section 9.1 is confined to unvested equity-scheme entitlements; hedging of vested holdings is expressly permitted with clearance, so a collar over vested shares is not categorically barred. Section 9.2 similarly permits the loan leg (margin loan or other secured lending arrangement) with the same clearance, and a lender's forced sale on default is excluded from Prohibited Period restrictions, giving the bank a workable enforcement path. Short-term or speculative trading is banned outright in section 10 with no clearance carve-out referenced, so tenor and any early unwind should avoid that characterisation, and clearance (valid 5 business days) can be withdrawn by the Approving Officer at any time before execution if circumstances change. Overall, the structure is workable subject to case-by-case Approving Officer discretion at both entry and unwind.
